demandEvidence: Filed as a concrete GitHub issue (runner-plugin issue #514, cited in the FEAT body) rather than 'users would like'. Live corroboration during THIS PM dispatch: the mcp__plugin_crew_astramem__recall_memory call I issued for this very review timed out after 300s with no response/progress before erroring — the exact 'opaque failure instead of a fast, actionable message' pattern the FEAT describes, reproduced in real time rather than hypothesized.
scopeNotes: Smallest deliverable: one small test-infra helper (e.g. under src/tests/lib/ or a shared e2e setup file) that does a raw `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:7777/health', { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(N) })`, maps the response into fail-fast vs proceed, plus the ASTRAMEM_E2E env-toggle branch and a docs paragraph. If forced to halve scope: keep the health GET + timeout + actionable message, drop the ASTRAMEM_E2E skip/require toggle to a follow-up — but the FEAT explicitly asks for both together and they are cheap to co-deliver, so no need to cut here. Overlap check: src/scripts/lib/memory-doctor.mts already exports probeMemory(), a CLI-based health diagnostic (spawns `astramem doctor --json`, 3s AbortController timeout) used by the runner's own dispatch/close ceremony (src/tests/memory-doctor.test.mts pins its cases). It is NOT a duplicate of this FEAT's ask: its own header comment states the doctor --json payload 'never reports whether the local/saas probe actually succeeded' and mapDoctorOutput() 'never returns ok' by design — it cannot answer 'is the daemon actually up' the way a direct GET /health can. FEAT-263 targets a different seam (MCP-tool e2e test preflight, HTTP-direct) and is complementary, not redundant; the builder should reference memory-doctor.mts's AbortController-timeout pattern for consistency but must not conflate the two health signals. AC clarity: original FEAT body prose was scope-clear but not testable Given-When-Then; ACs rewritten inline below per the AC quality checklist (concrete timeout/status/env values, explicit edge/error coverage). Weak-dimension check (Framework 4): loop-snapshot.md's last-5 grade averages are all >= 0.80 (architecture_quality 0.846, reliability 0.86, observability 0.82, production_readiness 0.872, security 0.88, test_confidence 0.914, product_completeness 0.844) — no weak dimension currently active, so no mandatory weak-dimension AC was required; AC-7 (docs) and the timeout-bound AC were added anyway on general test-reliability grounds. Effort analog (Framework 5): closest comparable is FEAT-244/SLICE-148 (single-repo, non-aggregate, $10.30 / 43 min, small single-purpose module) — a similarly-scoped single-helper-plus-docs slice; effort_estimate 0.2 is consistent with that analog. FEAT-257/SLICE-159 ($140/52min) was also reviewed but rejected as an analog — it's a 4-source aggregate cross-repo provider-migration slice, an order of magnitude larger scope than a single health-check helper.
risks: The exact GET /health response contract (status field name, the {ok,starting,degraded} enum, path) is taken from FEAT-263's prose, not verified against astramem-local's actual server source (that package lives outside this repo's tree — no /health route was found under src/ or docs/ here). If the real daemon's health payload shape differs, the builder's parsing logic will silently produce false negatives/positives; the builder should confirm the contract against the astramem-local source or a live daemon response before finalizing, and AC-1/AC-3 should be treated as provisional on that confirmation.

Default-to-skip semantics for an unset/falsy ASTRAMEM_E2E could mask a genuinely broken daemon in CI if no CI lane ever sets ASTRAMEM_E2E=require — the memory e2e suite would report all-green while silently never having exercised the daemon path. Recommend at least one CI lane (or a documented local pre-push step) runs with ASTRAMEM_E2E=require so regressions in this preflight itself get caught.

Coverage gap: none of the existing tests (memory-doctor.test.mts covers the CLI-based probeMemory() path only) would catch a regression in a new direct-HTTP health check — this is a genuinely new code path with zero existing test coverage, so the slice's own AC (and resulting tests) are the only backstop; no pre-mortem template was mandatory here (technical_risk 0.3, priority P2) but this gap is worth naming since it's a net-new external-call code path.

Effort well under the 8-point decomposition-gate threshold, so no proposedSlices emitted.
acs: AC-1: Given the astramem-local daemon is listening and healthy on 127.0.0.1:7777, When the e2e preflight helper issues a GET to `http://127.0.0.1:7777/health` with a short timeout (e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(2000)`), Then it resolves successfully and the memory e2e suite proceeds because the reported status is one of `ok`, `starting`, or `degraded`.

AC-2: Given the astramem-local daemon is NOT running on 127.0.0.1:7777, When the preflight helper runs before the memory e2e suite, Then the call fails fast (bounded by the configured timeout, not left to the OS-level connect timeout) and the failure surfaces an actionable message instructing the operator to start the daemon via `node dist/cli/index.js reinstall` or `serve --port 7777`, instead of an opaque `ECONNREFUSED` stack trace.

AC-3: Given the daemon responds to GET /health but reports a status outside `{ok, starting, degraded}` (e.g. `error` or an unrecognized string), When the preflight helper evaluates the response body, Then it treats this the same as an unreachable daemon (fails fast with the same actionable start-command message from AC-2), not a generic JSON-parse or type error.

AC-4: Given `ASTRAMEM_E2E` is unset, or set to `skip`/`0`/`false`, When the memory e2e test suite starts, Then the daemon preflight and every memory-dependent test in the suite are skipped (reported as skipped, not failed or errored) and no network request to 127.0.0.1:7777 is made.

AC-5: Given `ASTRAMEM_E2E` is set to `require`/`1`/`true` and the daemon preflight fails (per AC-2 or AC-3), When the memory e2e suite runs, Then the run fails loudly with a non-zero exit / failing test carrying the actionable message, rather than silently skipping.

AC-6: Given the daemon port is unreachable (nothing listening on 127.0.0.1:7777), When the preflight helper's GET /health call is issued, Then the call resolves or rejects within the documented short timeout window and never hangs indefinitely — regression-guards the exact failure mode observed live during this PM review, where an astramem MCP call hung 300s with no response.

AC-7: Given a contributor wants to run the memory e2e suite for the first time, When they read the updated test docs (e.g. `docs/sop/memory-bridge.md` or an equivalent e2e-setup doc), Then the docs explicitly state the 127.0.0.1:7777 daemon dependency, the exact start commands (`node dist/cli/index.js reinstall`, `serve --port 7777`), and the accepted `ASTRAMEM_E2E` values (`skip` vs `require`) with their default behavior.
